ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, point $P$ is the midpoint of diagonal $BD$, points $E$ and $F$ are the midpoints of $AB$ and $CD$, respectively, $AD=BC$, $\angle CBD=30^\circ$, and $\angle ADB=100^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle PFE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since point P is the midpoint of BD, and point E is the midpoint of AB,\\
it follows that PE is the midline of $\triangle ABD$,\\
therefore PE=$\frac{1}{2}$AD, PE$\parallel$AD,\\
thus $\angle$EPD=$180^\circ-\angle$ADB=$80^\circ$,\\
Similarly, PF=$\frac{1}{2}$BC, PF$\parallel$BC,\\
thus $\angle$FPD=$\angle$CBD=$30^\circ$,\\
since AD=BC,\\
it follows that PE=PF,\\
thus $\angle$PFE=$\frac{1}{2}\times(180^\circ-110^\circ)=\boxed{35^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is quadrilateral ABCD, A and B are at the two ends of the bottom side, D and C are above, and diagonal BD is drawn; P is located on BD, E is located on AB, F is located on CD, and PE, PF, FE are connected in the figure. The problem statement gives that P is the midpoint of BD, E and F are respectively the midpoints of AB and CD, and AD=BC, ∠ADB=100°, ∠CBD=30°. Reasoning: In triangle ABD, P is the midpoint of BD, and E is the midpoint of AB, so PE is the midline of triangle ABD. Therefore PE ∥ AD, and PE=AD/2. Since ray PD is opposite in direction to DB, and ∠ADB is the angle formed by AD and DB at point D, ∠EPD=180°−100°=80°. In triangle CBD, P is the midpoint of BD, and F is the midpoint of CD, so PF is the midline of triangle CBD. Therefore PF ∥ BC, and PF=BC/2. Also because ∠CBD is the included angle of BC and BD, and PD corresponds to BD in the same direction, to the direction from B pointing to D, ∠FPD=30°. From AD=BC, it can be obtained that PE=AD/2=BC/2=PF. Therefore triangle PEF is an isosceles triangle, and the vertex angle ∠EPF=∠EPD+∠DPF=80°+30°=110°. So the base angle ∠PFE=(180°−110°)/2=35°.
